Prefer event-driven native wait_agent waiting over timed polling. First confirm the current Host's actual maximum, meaningful-event early return, user interruption and child notification capabilities; unconfirmed capabilities remain UNKNOWN. When meaningful-event early return is confirmed and no dependency needs an interim decision, default to the supported 60-minute window (timeout_ms=3600000). This is a maximum waiting window, not a required execution duration; native completion wakes Controller early. Short historical averages must not force an earlier wake. If timed stage checks are needed or early return is unreliable, recommend 60 seconds for very short tasks, 10–60 minutes for ordinary tasks by work scale, and about 30 minutes for longer-task stage checks; reliable events without interim decisions still favor 60 minutes. Actual tool limits, explicit applicable higher-level duration limits, user interruption, recovery and urgent decisions take precedence; never bypass Host limits. Distinguish native terminal evidence from ordinary child messages and timeouts: messages and timeouts do not prove completion. A wake-only result needs one available exact native status check. Use a completed result directly without confirming the same completion again. Do not substitute sleep, add progress pollers, create per-child timed polling loops or repeatedly wake models for unchanged state. Executors own local tests and CI; independent closing owns final acceptance.
